pale overcast sky / municipal paper field

lighting: Flat winter daylight: soft, overcast, low-contrast, with no theatrical spotlights. Keep the hero field bright but cold; let brick and fence marks carry darker density. Small window glints may be milky or greenish, like daylight caught in old glass.
object_inventory: Two major structures: a large pale negative field and one lower architectural facade/slab. Secondary marks should be sparse and legible, arranged as window stacks, sign slit, fence rail, curb seam, and a few torn-paper/poster chips.

Make the anchor article visible through the architecture itself: 6–10 real source windows should read as facade apertures, bay-window panes, a vertical sign cut, fence gaps, snow/curb notches, road-stripe seams, and small compliance-paper repairs. One or two hero-scale source marks can be a large blank window panel or oversized sign-slit; smaller sources can live as pinholes, glints, chips, and edge cuts. Avoid separate cards floating on top of the image.
negative_constraints: no equal-weight grid of source objects
no unrelated replacement image or metaphorical scene when a source image is attached

Do not repeat a bleached timber section or literal cutaway diagram as the main look.
